subject: Immediate: Polaris Health — rate suppression causing production errors
messages:
From: Julie Tan <julie.tan@polarishealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@polarishealth.com
Date: 2028-11-06T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Production errors and token rejections since 08:30 PT

Hannah,

We started seeing a sudden spike in 5xx responses and elevated latencies across our endpoints around 08:30 PT this morning. Throughput dropped by ~25% and a subset of requests are returning rate_limit_exceeded errors (see sample traces attached).

Impact: our clinician-facing triage UI slowed and several background jobs retried aggressively. We have a critical window this afternoon (11:00–13:00 PT) where throughput must be stable.

Attached: logs_polaris_1106.zip with request IDs and sample payloads.

Can you triage urgently and let us know if this is on our side or something in your rate/quota config?

Julie
Julie Tan
Head of Platform, Polaris Health
julie.tan@polarishealth.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Tan <julie.tan@polarishealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-06T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and token rejections since 08:30 PT

Julie — thanks for the quick signal and the logs. I'm escalating to SRE and CS. Dylan, can you triage the logs attached and confirm whether this looks like a rate/quotas issue vs model-side errors?

Polaris — immediate plan:
- Dylan to run a throttling audit on Polaris's dedicated pool (will check burst windows and quota inheritance).
- I will apply a temporary override if we find a conservative misconfiguration to get them through the noon window.
- We'll follow up with a short post-incident review and propose a permanent policy fix.

Dylan/Marissa/Laura — please keep Polaris in the loop. I want an ETA for a mitigative action within 45 minutes if possible.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-06T10:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and token rejections since 08:30 PT

Quick findings from the attached logs and control plane:
- Observed spike in token rejections correlated with a burst window enforcement kicking in at 08:29 PT.
- Polaris's account was running a legacy quota profile that inherits from the org default. The org default has a "burst_window_sec" set to 60 (1m) with a conservative burst_capacity. For Polaris's traffic pattern (frequent short bursts over 15m), the 1m window is too narrow and causes token bucket exhaustion.
- There is also a mismatch between the console UI and API: the UI showed "Burst: liberal" for Polaris, but the API payload linked to their quota_policy referenced the org default. I suspect a deployment-time migration bug when we rolled quota inheritance last quarter.

Immediate mitigation (proposed):
1) Apply temporary override to Polaris quota_policy to set burst_window_sec=600 and burst_capacity=4x for the next 24 hours.
2) Enable verbose throttling logs for their pool and increase KV-cache for common prefixes to reduce request load.
3) Monitor: we should see token rejections subside within 2–3 minutes post-change.

Command I would run (ops runway):
- POST /admin/quotas/override {"account":"polaris-health", "burst_window_sec":600, "burst_capacity":40, "ttl_sec":86400}  <-- override_command.txt attached

I'll apply this if we have sign-off from Hannah/Marissa. I do not see model errors in the trace; latency spikes appear downstream of the throttling gates.

- Dylan
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Tan <julie.tan@polarishealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-06T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and token rejections since 08:30 PT

Julie — quick update: our SRE team identified a quota inheritance mismatch that was causing an overly narrow burst window to be enforced for your account. We've applied a temporary override to widen the burst window and bump burst capacity for the next 24 hours while we validate. Please let us know if the 5xxs stop or if you still see elevated latencies.

What we did:
- Temporary override applied (burst_window_sec=600, burst_capacity=40)
- Verbose throttling logs enabled for your pool
- Monitoring dashboard: https://internal.redwood.ai/dashboards/polaris-throttle (watching errors/latency now)

Next steps for joint action:
- Dylan will monitor for the next 12 hours and revert to a permanent change only after post-incident review.
- We'll schedule a 45-min post-mortem tomorrow to review root cause and UI/API mismatch.
- If there is measurable customer impact, we'll follow Redwood's crediting playbook.

Julie — can you confirm whether the error rate decreased after 11:05?

Thanks,
Hannah

From: Julie Tan <julie.tan@polarishealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@polarishealth.com
Date: 2028-11-07T08:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and token rejections since 08:30 PT

Hannah — thanks for the rapid response. After the override the 5xxs dropped to near zero and latency stabilized for our peak window. We did see CPU utilization on a few worker nodes climb and one background job retried several times, but overall the clinician UI was functional.

What we need from Redwood:
- A permanent fix so this doesn't recur (we're concerned about the UI/API mismatch you mentioned).
- A short post-incident report (timeline, root cause, fix plan).
- Given the impact during our 11:00–13:00 PT window, our billing team requests a credit estimate; please provide your recommendation.

Julie

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-08T15:43:00-08:00
Subject: Polaris Health — exec note and proposed customer relief

Team — thanks for the quick containment work on Polaris. This has executive visibility; Polaris is a strategic account and we should move decisively. Proposed actions: 
1) Approve a one-time service credit of 10% of November billed usage (recommendation based on impacted window and retry costs). Laura, please draft the credit note and run it through Tax/Finance. (Attachment: draft_credit_note.docx)
2) Product to triage the UI/API quota inheritance mismatch immediately; open JIRA INF-1248 and assign a patch for the quota migration edge-case.
3) Ops/SRE: make the temporary override change persistent with safe defaults for dedicated accounts (we should not rely on ad-hoc overrides).
4) Schedule a 30-min customer-facing post-incident review this week and a 60-min internal blameless post-mortem.

Dylan — please include the metric set (throttle metrics screenshot attached) and a succinct timeline in the post-incident report. Hannah — I'll join the customer call if necessary.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
